rounds.summary: Fixed the broken order flow — the submit handler targeted a nonexistent id ('orderform' vs 'order-form') so every order was silently lost on submit — and now the button confirms inline with the order details plus required drink/name fields, so the site's single conversion action actually completes.

Made the page mobile-first (device-width viewport, fluid layout, full-width 16px touch-friendly form controls that survive 375px) and replaced the banned Comic Sans/marquee styling with a clean, trustworthy coffee-house design, because phone visitors currently get a zoomed-out 980px page nobody can order from; the working order form and its JS are untouched.
Replaced the free-text drink input with one-tap menu chips that show prices at the decision point, removing typing friction and typos from the order flow.

Added a sticky order bar that keeps the conversion action one tap away while scrolling, mirrors the selected drink and price so the next step feels concrete, and hides itself once the real submit button is on screen.

Closed the loop on the promo banner: added a one-tap muffin add-on chip and a live order total (with the 50¢ deal applied automatically) so the advertised offer is actually orderable and customers see the price before hitting submit.

Turned the static text menu into tap-to-order buttons that preselect that item in the form, reprice the live total and sticky bar, and scroll the visitor straight down to checkout — so browsing the menu converts into an order instead of a memory test.

Turned the sticky order bar into a live mini-cart: the picked items and running total now follow the visitor on every screen (and highlight once an order is started), so the price stays in view between menu tap and submit instead of living only inside the form.
